This paper asks whether strict-test acceptance is admissible on fixed support without repairing that bridge level. The method is a layer-local, audit-based PICA route: promotion, internalization of protocol coordinates, carrier exactification, and audited source admission produce a carrier substrate above the bridge-native level. On the resulting carriers, the readout-agreement, quadratic-witness, and transition-witness slots are strict-realized natively; the three-slot strict domain closes; and accepted scoped strict test families survive the required control panel. The panel covers null-baseline, memory-only, artifact, boundary, selected-lift, visibility, and claim-boundary checks. The bridge-native level is retained as the : descent from new-layer evidence to old-layer compatibility preserves non-factorization without inducing old-layer strict realization. The final classification is a strict theory extension at the new layer with old-layer real-provisional compatibility intact. The result is bounded: it does not assert event-package construction, shared-event identity, proto-effect or effect-algebra structure, Born valuation, composition readiness, faithful public compression, a lawful public carrier, or canonical selected lifts.

resolved_source_locations.conclusion: Six Birds Foundations I introduced a stratified closure calculus with six primitive closure roles. The present paper extends that calculus into a theorem-level framework in three parts: a primitive role architecture fixing the meanings, levels, local boundaries, and selected lifts of the six typed closure roles P_1, ,P_6 ; an admissibility and meta-theory regime in which honest bookkeeping, typed non-collapse, level profiles, forgetting with selected lifts, activation thresholds, instrument-relative visibility, and empirical-bridge admissibility are stated as theorem schemas; and a scoped exact-six theorem chain over the domain of finite audited typed closure descriptions. Within this domain we prove six role-lower-bound witnesses, an upper-bound classification with corrected role-projection alignments (closing the probability, causality, and agency threats in the covered scope), a decomposition/exhaustion theorem, and an integrated stress certification. The terminal theorem asserts that every D admits a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion record with exactly six role channels, each in one of five recorded statuses, with residual features classified under an explicit scheme and, under an explicit recognition hypothesis (the three principal threat classes — probability, causality, and agency — closed unconditionally), no seventh irreducible role required in the covered scope. The claim concerns role channels rather than active projections, and the decomposition is existential, not unique. We do not claim unrestricted exact-six, all-emergence coverage, a full six-primitives algebra, global primitive independence, empirical realization, internal instrument-family completeness, or recognition-completeness of the six roles.
